claim: The majority of multi-spanning membrane proteins are co-translationally inserted into the bilayer by the Sec pathway.
source: The majority of multi-spanning membrane proteins are co-translationally inserted into the bilayer by the Sec pathway.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge about membrane protein insertion.

claim: An important subset of membrane proteins have globular, cofactor-containing extracytoplasmic domains requiring the dual action of the co-translational Sec and post-translational Tat pathways for integration.
source: An important subset of membrane proteins have globular, cofactor-containing extracytoplasmic domains requiring the dual action of the co-translational Sec and post-translational Tat pathways for integration.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract.

claim: A predicted heme-molybdenum cofactor-containing protein requires the concerted action of two translocases for assembly.
source: We establish that a predicted heme-molybdenum cofactor-containing protein, and a complex polyferredoxin, each require the concerted action of two translocases for their assembly.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in the results section.

claim: A complex polyferredoxin requires the concerted action of two translocases for assembly.
source: We establish that a predicted heme-molybdenum cofactor-containing protein, and a complex polyferredoxin, each require the concerted action of two translocases for their assembly.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in the results section.

claim: The mechanism of handover from Sec to Tat pathway requires the relatively low hydrophobicity of the Tat-dependent transmembrane domain.
source: We determine that the mechanism of handover from Sec to Tat pathway requires the relatively low hydrophobicity of the Tat-dependent transmembrane domain.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data showing that increasing hydrophobicity increases Sec-dependent insertion.

claim: The presence of C-terminal positive charges results in abortive insertion of the Tat-dependent transmembrane domain by the Sec pathway.
source: This, coupled with the presence of C-terminal positive charges, results in abortive insertion of this transmembrane domain by the Sec pathway and its subsequent release at the cytoplasmic side of the membrane.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data showing that removal or addition of positive charges affects Sec-dependent insertion.

claim: Prokaryotic cytoplasmic membrane proteins represent 20–30% of the proteome.
source: Prokaryotic cytoplasmic membrane proteins represent 20–30% of the proteome (Wallin and von Heijne, 1998; Krogh et al., 2001)
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The SecYEG translocon is the major route by which multi-spanning membrane proteins are integrated into the membrane.
source: The SecYEG translocon is the major route by which multi-spanning membrane proteins are integrated into the membrane.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: The insertion of transmembrane domains of polytopic proteins occurs co-translationally following targeting of the translating ribosome to the Sec machinery through the action of signal recognition particle (SRP).
source: The insertion of transmembrane domains of polytopic proteins occurs co-translationally following targeting of the translating ribosome to the Sec machinery through the action of signal recognition particle (SRP) (Ulbrandt et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: YidC is positioned close to the lateral gate of SecY and interacts with nascent transmembrane domains to facilitate their integration into the membrane.
source: YidC is positioned close to the lateral gate of SecY and interacts with nascent transmembrane domains to facilitate their integration into the membrane (Scotti et al., 2000; Urbanus et al., 2001; Sachelaru et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: YidC can act independently of the Sec system to integrate small (usually mono- or bitopic) membrane proteins directly into the bilayer.
source: YidC can also act independently of the Sec system to integrate small (usually mono- or bitopic) membrane proteins directly into the bilayer (Dalbey et al., 2014; Samuelson et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The Tat system is a post-translational protein transport pathway that operates independently of the Sec and YidC machineries to transport folded proteins across the cytoplasmic membrane.
source: The Tat system is a post-translational protein transport pathway that operates independently of the Sec and YidC machineries to transport folded proteins across the cytoplasmic membrane (reviewed in Berks, 2015; Kudva et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to review articles.

claim: Proteins are targeted to the Tat machinery by N-terminal signal sequences containing a highly conserved pair of arginine residues that are usually critical for efficient recognition of substrates.
source: Proteins are targeted to the Tat machinery by N-terminal signal sequences containing a highly conserved pair of arginine residues that are usually critical for efficient recognition of substrates (Stanley et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: A subset of Tat substrate proteins contain non-covalently bound prosthetic groups such as metal-sulphur clusters or nucleotide-based cofactors, many of which play important roles in respiratory and photosynthetic metabolism.
source: A subset of Tat substrate proteins contain non-covalently bound prosthetic groups such as metal-sulphur clusters or nucleotide-based cofactors, many of which play important roles in respiratory and photosynthetic metabolism (Palmer and Berks, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The actinobacterial Rieske proteins have three transmembrane domains (TMDs) preceding the Rieske FeS domain.
source: The actinobacterial proteins have three transmembrane domains (TMDs) preceding the Rieske FeS domain, unlike most other Rieske proteins which contain only one TMD.
evidence: This is stated as an observation about actinobacterial Rieske proteins.

claim: Most other Rieske proteins contain only one TMD.
source: The actinobacterial proteins have three transmembrane domains (TMDs) preceding the Rieske FeS domain, unlike most other Rieske proteins which contain only one TMD.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison to actinobacterial Rieske proteins.

claim: The first two TMDs of the Streptomyces coelicolor Rieske protein, Sco2149, are inserted by the Sec machinery.
source: Indeed it was shown that the first two TMDs of the Streptomyces coelicolor Rieske protein, Sco2149, are inserted by the Sec machinery, probably in a co-translational manner, whereas the insertion of TMD3 is dependent on the Tat pathway (Keller et al., 2012)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The insertion of TMD3 of Sco2149 is dependent on the Tat pathway.
source: Indeed it was shown that the first two TMDs of the Streptomyces coelicolor Rieske protein, Sco2149, are inserted by the Sec machinery, probably in a co-translational manner, whereas the insertion of TMD3 is dependent on the Tat pathway (Keller et al., 2012)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Actinobacterial Rieske proteins provide the first example of the Sec and Tat machineries operating together to assemble a single protein.
source: Indeed it was shown that the first two TMDs of the Streptomyces coelicolor Rieske protein, Sco2149, are inserted by the Sec machinery, probably in a co-translational manner, whereas the insertion of TMD3 is dependent on the Tat pathway (Keller et al., 2012), providing the first example of these two machineries operating together to assemble a single protein.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the cited study.

claim: There are at least two further conserved families of dual targeted membrane proteins across bacteria and archaea that each have 5 TMDs.
source: Here we have addressed both of these major aspects and show that in addition to Rieske there are at least two further conserved families of dual targeted membrane proteins across bacteria and archaea that each have 5 TMDs.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the introduction and supported by bioinformatic analysis and experimental data.

claim: A further family of proteins related to the Bacillus subtilis Tat substrate YkuE and predicted to have 4TMDs was identified.
source: A further family of proteins related to the Bacillus subtilis Tat substrate YkuE (Monteferrante et al., 2012) and predicted to have 4TMDs was also identified.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the introduction and supported by bioinformatic analysis.

claim: The relatively low hydrophobicity of TMD3 coupled with the location of positively charged amino acid residues orchestrate the release of the polypeptide by the Sec pathway.
source: A detailed dissection of the features of the transmembrane regions of S. coelicolor Rieske reveals that the relatively low hydrophobicity of TMD3 coupled with the location of positively charged amino acid residues orchestrate the release of the polypeptide by the Sec pathway.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the introduction and supported by experimental data.

claim: The features governing Sec-Tat handover are present across all identified families of dual-targeted membrane proteins.
source: Importantly, we demonstrate that these features are also present across all identified families of these dual-targeted membrane proteins indicating that there is unifying mechanism for their biogenesis.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the introduction and supported by experimental data and sequence analysis.

claim: When plasmid-encoded native AmiA or the Sco2149TMD-AmiA fusion was produced in the tat+ strain lacking chromosomally encoded periplasmic AmiA and AmiC (MCDSSAC), growth on SDS was restored.
source: As expected, when either plasmid-encoded native AmiA or the Sco2149TMD-AmiA fusion was produced in the tat+ strain lacking chromosomally encoded periplasmic AmiA and AmiC (MCDSSAC), growth on SDS was restored (Figure 1C, middle two panels).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The export of AmiA from Sco2149TMD-AmiA was absolutely dependent on the Tat pathway.
source: The export of AmiA from both of these constructs was absolutely dependent on the Tat pathway as no growth on SDS was conferred in the tat- strain (MCDSSAC △tat).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: There is some compatibility of TMD3 of the S. coelicolor Rieske protein with the Sec pathway.
source: Taken together these results indicate that there is some compatibility of TMD3 of the S. coelicolor Rieske protein with the Sec pathway, which was not seen previously using a more qualitative assay (Keller et al., 2012).
evidence: This is concluded from experimental data showing Sec-dependent export of Bla in a tat- strain.

claim: Substitution of the twin arginines to alanine-aspartate reduced the MIC for ampicillin to near basal level.
source: As shown in Figure 1D these substitutions reduced the MIC for ampicillin to 4.0 and 1.3 µg/ml, respectively, for tat+ and tat- strain, very close to basal level.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: None of the substitutions in the cytoplasmic loop region had any substantive effect on the interaction of Sco2149 with the Sec pathway, except for the introduction of an alanine-aspartate pair to replace the twin arginines.
source: As shown in Table 1, apart from the introduction of an alanine-aspartate pair to replace the twin arginines, none of the substitutions we introduced, including replacement of the highly conserved E127 or R133/H134 residues or introduction of proline residues into the predicted α-helical region, had any substantive effect on the interaction of Sco2149 with the Sec pathway.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Table 1.

claim: Most of the truncations in the cytoplasmic loop region had little effect on translocation of Sco2149TMD-Bla by the Sec pathway.
source: Again most of the truncations had little effect on translocation of Sco2149TMD-Bla by the Sec pathway, and even truncations of 30 residues or more gave mean M.I.C.s for ampicillin similar to that seen for the non-mutated construct.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Table 2.

claim: Many of the conserved features in the Sco2149 cytoplasmic loop region do not modulate interaction of Sco2149 with the Sec pathway.
source: These findings indicate that many of the conserved features noted in this loop region, for example the overall length, presence of a predicted α-helical region and clusters of negatively charged amino acids do not modulate interaction of Sco2149 with the Sec pathway.
evidence: This is concluded from the mutagenesis data in Tables 1 and 2.

claim: The Tat system was still able to identify and integrate TMD3 when the cytoplasmic loop was truncated by up to 30 residues.
source: The loop truncation experiments indicated that the Tat system was still able to identify and integrate TMD3 when it was truncated by up to 30 residues.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Table 2.

claim: A minimum loop length requirement of approximately eight amino acids between TMD2 and the twin arginine motif is required for Tat recognition of a tethered signal peptide.
source: However, one of the 35 residue truncations (Sco2149TMD-Δ123–157-AmiA) and the 40 residue truncation (Sco2149TMD-Δ118–157-AmiA) supported no growth on SDS-containing media (Table 2; Figure 1—figure supplement 4), indicating that there is a minimum loop length requirement of approximately eight amino acids between TMD2 and the twin arginine motif is required for Tat recognition of a tethered signal peptide.
evidence: This is concluded from experimental data shown in Table 2 and Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: With the exception of the twin arginine motif, none of the conserved features of cytoplasmic loop are strictly necessary for interaction of Sco2149 with the Tat pathway or to mediate release from Sec.
source: Taken together we conclude that, with the exception of the twin arginine motif, none of the conserved features of cytoplasmic loop are strictly necessary for interaction of Sco2149 with the Tat pathway or to mediate release from Sec.
evidence: This is concluded from the mutagenesis data in Tables 1 and 2.

claim: The first and last TMDs of polytopic proteins are notably more hydrophobic than the central helices.
source: Analysis of transmembrane helices from polytopic proteins of known three-dimensional structure shows a general trend that the first and last TMDs are of similar hydrophobicity, and they are notably more hydrophobic than the central helices (Hedin et al., 2010; Virkki et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The first and second TMDs of actinobacterial Rieske proteins have negative predicted △Gapp values and are therefore expected to be inserted as TMDs by the Sec system.
source: It can be seen that the first and second TMDs have negative predicted △Gapp values and are therefore expected to be inserted as TMDs by the Sec system (Ojemalm et al., 2013).
evidence: This is based on analysis of predicted △Gapp values shown in Table 3 and supported by a citation.

claim: The third TMD of actinobacterial Rieske proteins is predicted to have a positive Gapp.
source: However, the third and final TMD is predicted to have a positive Gapp (Table 3).
evidence: This is based on analysis of predicted △Gapp values shown in Table 3.

claim: TMD3 of actinobacterial Rieske proteins might be poorly recognised by the Sec machinery.
source: This is in contrast to the final TMD of 'standard' Sec-dependent proteins and suggests that this helix might be poorly recognised by the Sec machinery.
evidence: This is inferred from the positive △Gapp value of TMD3.

claim: Substitution of a single leucine residue at either serine 179 or glycine 180 reduces the predicted △Gapp value for TMD3 Sec-dependent membrane insertion by at least 0.6 kcal mol−1.
source: Table 3 shows that substitution of a single leucine residue at either serine 179 or glycine 180 reduces the predicted △Gapp value for TMD3 Sec-dependent membrane insertion by at least 0.6 kcal mol−1.
evidence: This is based on analysis of predicted △Gapp values shown in Table 3.

claim: Single leucine substitutions at S179 or G180 in Sco2149TMD-Bla dramatically increased the M.I.C for ampicillin up to 25 fold in tat- cells.
source: Accordingly, when these single substitutions were individually introduced into the Sco2149TMD-Bla fusion in tat- cells, a dramatic increase in M.I.C for ampicillin of up to 25 fold was observed (Figure 3B), almost at the upper limit of detection.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The low hydrophobicity of TMD3 is a key driver for the release of Sco2149 from the Sec machinery.
source: We conclude that the low hydrophobicity of TMD3 is a key driver for the release of Sco2149 from the Sec machinery.
evidence: This is concluded from experimental data showing that increasing hydrophobicity increases Sec-dependent insertion.

claim: Tat signal peptides frequently contain one or more positive charges in their c-regions, close to the site of signal peptidase cleavage.
source: It has long been known that Tat signal peptides frequently contain one or more positive charges in their c-regions, close to the site of signal peptidase cleavage.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Positive charges in Tat signal peptides are not required for the interaction with the Tat pathway but reduce the efficiency of interaction with Sec.
source: These charges are not required for the interaction with the Tat pathway but reduce the efficiency of interaction with Sec and have therefore been described 'Sec-avoidance' motifs (Bogsch et al., 1997; Cristóbal et al., 1999; Blaudeck et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: A positive charge is generally found close to the C-terminal end of TMD3 of actinobacterial Rieske proteins.
source: A positive charge is generally also found close to the C-terminal end of TMD3 of actinobacterial Rieske proteins (R185 in the case of Sco2149; Figure 3A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis shown in Figure 3A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: There are a number of non-conserved positive charges located within the C-terminal vicinity of TMD3 of actinobacterial Rieske proteins.
source: Interestingly, closer inspection of actinobacterial Rieske proteins indicates that there are a number of further non-conserved positive charges located within the C-terminal vicinity of TMD3 (Figure 3A underlined residues, Figure 1—figure supplement 1 orange residues) which are not found in other Rieske proteins that only contain a single TMD (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis shown in Figure 3A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Inclusion of additional positively charged residues C-terminal to TMD3 almost completely abolished transport via Sec.
source: It can be seen that inclusion of this additional positively charged stretch almost completely abolished transport via Sec, as the clearance zone around the M.I.C. strip was of similar size to that of the negative control (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: A combination of low hydrophobicity of TMD3 coupled with the presence of several C-terminal positive charges promotes release of actinobacterial Rieske proteins from the Sec machinery.
source: Taken together, we conclude that a combination of low hydrophobicity of TMD3 coupled with the presence of several C-terminal positive charges promotes release of actinobacterial Rieske proteins from the Sec machinery.
evidence: This is concluded from experimental data showing effects of hydrophobicity and positive charges on Sec-dependent insertion.

claim: Sco3746 from S. coelicolor is predicted to have five TMDs, with a predicted molybdenum cofactor (MoCo) binding domain at the C-terminus.
source: Sco3746, also from S. coelicolor is predicted to have five TMDs, with a predicted molybdenum cofactor (MoCo) binding domain at the C-terminus and conserved histidine residues in TMDs 2, 3 and 4 that are predicted to co-ordinate two heme b moieties (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is based on bioinformatic analysis and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Sco3746 has conserved histidine residues in TMDs 2, 3 and 4 that are predicted to co-ordinate two heme b moieties.
source: Sco3746, also from S. coelicolor is predicted to have five TMDs, with a predicted molybdenum cofactor (MoCo) binding domain at the C-terminus and conserved histidine residues in TMDs 2, 3 and 4 that are predicted to co-ordinate two heme b moieties (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is based on bioinformatic analysis and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The twin arginine motif of Sco3746 directly precedes TMD5.
source: The twin arginine motif, which is conserved across homologous proteins (Figure 5), directly precedes TMD5.
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis shown in Figure 5.

claim: Homologues of Sco3746 were identified across the actinobacteria, as well as in firmicutes, chloroflexi and euryarchaeota.
source: Homologues of Sco3746 were identified across the actinobacteria, as well as in firmicutes, chloroflexi and euryarchaeota, and each carries a twin arginine motif directly preceding TMD5 (Examples from each phyla are shown in Figure 5).
evidence: This is based on bioinformatic analysis shown in Figure 5.

claim: Protein Q1NSB0 from the delta proteobacterium MLMS-1 is predicted to have five TMDs and to contain seven 4Fe-4S clusters.
source: Protein Q1NSB0 from the delta proteobacterium MLMS-1 is also predicted to have five TMDs and to contain seven 4Fe-4S clusters, three at the cytoplasmic side and four at the extracellular side of the membrane (Figure 4A; Figure 6).
evidence: This is based on bioinformatic analysis shown in Figure 4A and Figure 6.

claim: The conserved twin arginine motif of Q1NSB0 directly precedes TMD5.
source: Again the conserved twin arginine motif directly precedes TMD5 and homologues of this protein are encoded in many prokaryotic genomes including those from the chloroflexi, nitrospirae and euryarchaeota phyla (Figure 6).
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis shown in Figure 6.

claim: E. coli malE− cells harboring MBP fused to the TMD regions of Sco3746 or PFD decolorized maltose minimal medium containing the pH indicator dye bromocresol purple.
source: As shown in Figure 4C, E. coli malE− cells harboring MBP fused to these regions of either protein decolorized maltose minimal medium containing the pH indicator dye bromocresol purple.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The MBP portion of the Sco3746TMD-MBP and PFDTMD-MBP fusion proteins has been translocated to the periplasmic side of the membrane.
source: This indicates that the MBP portion of the fusion protein has been translocated to the periplasmic side of the membrane.
evidence: This is inferred from the maltose fermentation assay results.

claim: Substituting the twin-arginines to twin lysines in Sco3746TMD-MBP and PFDTMD-MBP abolished maltose fermentation.
source: This conservative substitution abolished maltose fermentation (Figure 4C), indicating that MBP translocation was dependent on the Tat pathway.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: MBP translocation from Sco3746TMD-MBP and PFDTMD-MBP was dependent on the Tat pathway.
source: This conservative substitution abolished maltose fermentation (Figure 4C), indicating that MBP translocation was dependent on the Tat pathway.
evidence: This is concluded from the twin lysine substitution experiment.

claim: When plasmid-encoded Sco3746TMD-AmiA or PFDTMD-AmiA was produced in the tat+ strain lacking native AmiA/C, growth on SDS was supported.
source: Figure 4D shows that, as expected, when either plasmid-encoded Sco3746TMD-AmiA or PFDTMD-AmiA was produced in the tat+ strain lacking native AmiA/C, growth on SDS was supported.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Export of AmiA from Sco3746TMD-AmiA and PFDTMD-AmiA was dependent on the Tat pathway.
source: Export was dependent on the Tat pathway since growth on SDS was not supported in the tat- strain, or in the tat+ strain if the twin arginine motif was substituted for twin lysine.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Sco3746 is dependent on the Tat pathway for its assembly.
source: We conclude that Sco3746 and PFD are dependent on the Tat pathway for their assembly.
evidence: This is concluded from the AmiA and MBP fusion experiments.

claim: PFD is dependent on the Tat pathway for its assembly.
source: We conclude that Sco3746 and PFD are dependent on the Tat pathway for their assembly.
evidence: This is concluded from the AmiA and MBP fusion experiments.

claim: Both Sco3746TMD-MBP and PFDTMD-MBP were detected exclusively in the membrane fraction of a tat+ strain.
source: Figure 8A shows that both Sco3746TMD-MBP and PFDTMD-MBP were detected exclusively in the membrane fraction of a tat+ strain at close to their theoretical masses (68 kDa for Sco3746TMD-MBP and 81 kDa for PFDTMD-MBP).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Substitution of the Tat consensus arginine pair for di-lysine did not detectably affect the amount of Sco3746TMD-MBP and PFDTMD-MBP fusion proteins produced, nor their membrane localization.
source: Substitution of the Tat consensus arginine pair for di-lysine did not detectably affect the amount of fusion proteins produced, nor their membrane localization, indicating that membrane insertion of each of these fusions occurred independently of the Tat system.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Membrane insertion of Sco3746TMD-MBP and PFDTMD-MBP occurred independently of the Tat system.
source: Substitution of the Tat consensus arginine pair for di-lysine did not detectably affect the amount of fusion proteins produced, nor their membrane localization, indicating that membrane insertion of each of these fusions occurred independently of the Tat system.
evidence: This is concluded from the observation that twin lysine substitution did not affect membrane localization.

claim: Sco3746TMD-MBP and PFDTMD-MBP were integrally inserted into the membrane in the absence of the Tat pathway.
source: Washing the membranes with 4 M urea or 0.2 M carbonate did not extract either protein (Figure 8B), indicating that they were integrally inserted into the membrane in the absence of the Tat pathway.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: The integral membrane insertion of Sco3746TMD-MBP and PFDTMD-MBP indicates the participation of a second protein translocase, almost certainly the Sec pathway.
source: This indicates the participation of a second protein translocase, almost certainly the Sec pathway, in the insertion of these proteins into the membrane.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that the proteins are membrane-inserted in the absence of Tat.

claim: The Sco3746TMD portion of the Sco3746TMD-MBP fusion has 5 TMDs.
source: Taken together we conclude that the Sco3746TMD portion of the Sco3746TMD-MBP fusion has 5 TMDs.
evidence: This is concluded from cysteine accessibility experiments shown in Figure 8D.

claim: Several non-conserved positive charges are located close to the C-terminus of TMD5 of the Sco3746 homologues.
source: Figure 5 shows that several non-conserved positive charges are located close to the C-terminus of TMD5 of the Sco3746 homologues examined, and analysis of predicted △Gapp values for membrane insertion of the five TMDs (Table 4) shows a positive △Gapp for TMD5 suggesting that it may potentially be poorly recognised by Sec.
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis shown in Figure 5.

claim: TMD5 of Sco3746 homologues has a positive △Gapp suggesting that it may potentially be poorly recognised by Sec.
source: Figure 5 shows that several non-conserved positive charges are located close to the C-terminus of TMD5 of the Sco3746 homologues examined, and analysis of predicted △Gapp values for membrane insertion of the five TMDs (Table 4) shows a positive △Gapp for TMD5 suggesting that it may potentially be poorly recognised by Sec.
evidence: This is based on analysis of predicted △Gapp values shown in Table 4.

claim: Substitution of two or more leucine residues into TMD5 of the short Sco3746TMD-Bla fusion doubled the M.I.C. for ampicillin.
source: Indeed, substitution of two or more leucine residues into the short fusion doubled the M.I.C. for ampicillin (Figure 9B), consistent with an increased level of insertion of TMD5 by Sec.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9B.

claim: The long Sco3746TMD-Bla fusion reduced the M.I.C. for ampicillin almost to the level of the empty vector control.
source: Figure 9B shows that this extension reduced the M.I.C. for ampicillin almost to the level of the empty vector control, consistent with the positive charges at the C-terminal end of Sco3746 TMD5 modulating interaction of this TMD with the Sec pathway.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9B.

claim: The positive charges at the C-terminal end of Sco3746 TMD5 modulate interaction of this TMD with the Sec pathway.
source: Figure 9B shows that this extension reduced the M.I.C. for ampicillin almost to the level of the empty vector control, consistent with the positive charges at the C-terminal end of Sco3746 TMD5 modulating interaction of this TMD with the Sec pathway.
evidence: This is concluded from the observation that adding positive charges reduces Sec-dependent insertion.

claim: All of the PFD proteins analysed have a non-conserved positively charged region at the C-terminal end of TMD5.
source: Similar to Sco3746 homologues, all of the PFD proteins analysed in Figure 6 also have a non-conserved positively charged region at the C-terminal end of TMD5.
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis shown in Figure 6.

claim: The Tat-dependent TMD of PFD proteins has a positive predicted △Gapp.
source: We therefore analysed only the first and fifth (Tat-dependent) TMDs (Table 5), and again it can be seen that the Tat-dependent TMD has a positive predicted △Gapp.
evidence: This is based on analysis of predicted △Gapp values shown in Table 5.

claim: Leucine substitutions in TMD5 of PFD significantly increased the level of interaction of the short fusion with the Sec pathway.
source: In agreement with this, Figure 10B shows that these substitutions significantly increased the level of interaction of the short fusion with the Sec pathway, giving mean M.I.C.s for ampicillin of 9.3 µg/ml for the G354L, R358L and 12.0 µg/ml for the G354L, P355L, R358L substitutions, respectively.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 10B.

claim: The same leucine substitutions confer lower levels of resistance to ampicillin when they are present in the long PFD construct than when they are in the short construct.
source: However it is clear that the same leucine substitutions confer lower levels of resistance to ampicillin when they are present in the long construct than when they are in the short construct (compare Figure 10B with Figure 10C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 10B and 10C.

claim: The additional positive charge present in the extended PFD fusion reduces the level of membrane insertion by Sec.
source: Since the shorter construct harbours one less positive charge at the C-terminal end of TMD5 we conclude that the additional positive charge present in the extended fusion reduces the level of membrane insertion by Sec.
evidence: This is concluded from comparing the short and long PFD fusion data.

claim: All of the YukE homologues analysed have a non-conserved positively charged region at the C-terminal end of TMD4.
source: Finally we noted that all of the YukE homologues we analysed in Figure 7 also have a non-conserved positively charged region at the C-terminal end of TMD4 that is not present in the shorter, soluble variants.
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis shown in Figure 7.

claim: The Tat-dependent TMD of YkuE homologues has a positive predicted △Gapp.
source: Moreover, analysis of predicted △Gapp values for membrane insertion of the TMDs (Table 6) again reveals that Tat-dependent TMD has a positive predicted △Gapp.
evidence: This is based on analysis of predicted △Gapp values shown in Table 6.

claim: The mechanism of Sec release of the final TMD is conserved across three families of dual Sec-Tat targeted membrane proteins.
source: Taken together our results demonstrate that the mechanism of Sec release of the final TMD is conserved across three families of dual Sec-Tat targeted membrane proteins.
evidence: This is concluded from the combined analysis of Rieske, Sco3746, and PFD proteins.

claim: None of the conserved features of the Sco2149 cytoplasmic loop region, other than the presence of one or more positively charged amino acids that serve as topology signals, plays any discernible role in co-ordinating the Sec and Tat pathways.
source: Here we show that that these principles are exploited by nature to regulate translocation of Rieske by the Sec pathway and allow its hand-off to Tat prior to insertion of the final TMD. None of the features of the highly conserved loop region, other than the presence of one or more positively charged amino acids that serve as topology signals, plays any discernible role in co-ordinating the Sec and Tat pathways and may therefore be required for cofactor insertion or interaction with other components of the cytochrome bc1 complex.
evidence: This is concluded from the mutagenesis experiments on the loop region.

claim: The conserved features of the Sco2149 cytoplasmic loop region may be required for cofactor insertion or interaction with other components of the cytochrome bc1 complex.
source: None of the features of the highly conserved loop region, other than the presence of one or more positively charged amino acids that serve as topology signals, plays any discernible role in co-ordinating the Sec and Tat pathways and may therefore be required for cofactor insertion or interaction with other components of the cytochrome bc1 complex.
evidence: This is speculated based on the observation that these features are conserved but not required for Sec-Tat coordination.

claim: The positively-charged twin-arginines N-terminal to the final TMD imposes an N-in, C-out orientation on this helix.
source: According to the model, the Sec-dependent helices are inserted co-translationally. The positively-charged twin-arginines N-terminal to the final TMD imposes an N-in, C-out orientation on this helix.
evidence: This is part of the proposed model based on the positive inside rule.

claim: The C-terminal positive charges prevent the full insertion of the final TMD because the relatively low hydrophobicity is insufficient to drive translocation of the C-terminal positively charged region.
source: However, the C-terminal positive charges prevent the full insertion of this TMD because the relatively low hydrophobicity is insufficient to drive translocation of the C-terminal positively charged region (Wahlberg and Spiess, 1997; Goder and Spiess, 2003).
evidence: This is part of the proposed model supported by experimental data and citations.

claim: The final TMD is likely released by the Sec pathway as a re-entrant loop.
source: Accordingly, it is likely that this final TMD is released by the Sec pathway as a re-entrant loop.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data and the proposed model.

claim: The Sec and Tat pathways of E. coli are able to co-operatively integrate dual-targeted protein families even though the organism itself does not encode such proteins.
source: However, it should be noted that the Sec and Tat pathways of E. coli are able to co-operatively integrate dual-targeted protein families even though the organism itself does not encode such proteins, suggesting that a direct Sec-Tat interaction is unlikely to be an essential feature of this process.
evidence: This is based on the observation that E. coli can integrate heterologous dual-targeted proteins.

claim: A direct Sec-Tat interaction is unlikely to be an essential feature of dual-targeted protein integration.
source: However, it should be noted that the Sec and Tat pathways of E. coli are able to co-operatively integrate dual-targeted protein families even though the organism itself does not encode such proteins, suggesting that a direct Sec-Tat interaction is unlikely to be an essential feature of this process.
evidence: This is inferred from the E. coli data.

claim: Signal peptides of soluble Tat substrates often contain one or more positively-charged residues in their c-regions which act as Sec-avoidance motifs.
source: Signal peptides of soluble Tat substrates often contain one or more positively-charged residues in their c-regions which are known to act as Sec-avoidance motifs. Removal of these charges results in signal sequences that can mediate efficient transport by the Sec machinery (Bogsch et al., 1997; Cristóbal et al., 1999; Blaudeck et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Tat signal peptides are less hydrophobic than Sec signal peptides.
source: Furthermore, signal peptides that direct proteins to the Tat machinery are known to be less hydrophobic than Sec signal peptides and if the hydrophobicity of a Tat signal peptide is increased it can also mediate efficient transport by the Sec pathway (Cristóbal et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Over half of the native E. coli Tat signal peptides are capable of transporting reporter proteins through the Sec pathway if fused to an appropriate passenger domain.
source: However, despite possessing these 'Sec-avoidance' features, over half of the native E. coli Tat signal peptides are capable of transporting reporter proteins through the Sec pathway if fused to an appropriate passenger domain (Tullman-Ercek et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Sec interaction with Tat signal peptides may be more frequent than previously thought.
source: This raises the possibility that rather than being an exception, Sec interaction with Tat signal peptides is much more frequent, and that following abortive attempts at Sec-translocation, membrane-associated twin-arginine signal peptides are common substrates of the Tat pathway.
evidence: This is speculated based on the observation that many Tat signal peptides can interact with Sec.

claim: Both thylakoid and E. coli Tat substrates interact with the membrane before subsequent interaction with Tat machinery.
source: In this context it should be noted that both thylakoid and E. coli Tat substrates interact with the membrane before subsequent interaction with Tat machinery (Musser and Theg, 2000; Ma and Cline, 2000; Shanmugham et al., 2006; Bageshwar et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Dual targeted Sec-Tat dependent membrane proteins are dispersed across two domains including Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria and euryarchaea.
source: Our work has shown that dual targeted Sec-Tat dependent membrane proteins are dispersed across two domains including Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria and euryarchaea, indicating that the biogenesis of dual-targeted membrane proteins is a common feature of prokaryotes.
evidence: This is based on the bioinformatic analysis identifying these proteins across diverse organisms.

claim: The biogenesis of dual-targeted membrane proteins is a common feature of prokaryotes.
source: Our work has shown that dual targeted Sec-Tat dependent membrane proteins are dispersed across two domains including Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria and euryarchaea, indicating that the biogenesis of dual-targeted membrane proteins is a common feature of prokaryotes.
evidence: This is concluded from the widespread distribution of these proteins.

claim: E. coli MsrP/MsrQ are, respectively, a Sec-dependent polytopic heme b protein and Tat-targeted soluble MoCo-containing periplasmic protein that together use electrons from the respiratory chain to catalyse the repair of proteins containing methionine sulfoxide.
source: For example E. coli MsrP/MsrQ (formerly YedY/YedZ encoded by yedYZ) are, respectively, a Sec-dependent polytopic heme b protein and Tat-targeted soluble MoCo-containing periplasmic protein that together use electrons from the respiratory chain to catalyse the repair of proteins containing methionine sulfoxide (Brokx et al., 2005; Gennaris et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: MLMS-1 polyferredoxin is a fusion of NapH and NapG.
source: Likewise MLMS-1 polyferredoxin is a fusion of NapH, a Sec-dependent polytopic protein with four TMD that co-ordinates [4Fe-4S] iron-sulfur clusters at the cytoplasmic side of the membrane, with NapG, a Tat-dependent periplasmic protein that is predicted to co-ordinate four [4Fe-4S] at the periplasmic side of the membrane.
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis and comparison to known proteins.

claim: NapGH form a quinol dehydrogenase complex that in E. coli and Wolinella succinogenes is involved in nitrate respiration.
source: Collectively NapGH form a quinol dehydrogenase complex that in E. coli and Wolinella succinogenes is involved in nitrate respiration (Brondijk et al., 2004; Kern and Simon, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Dual-targeted proteins may have arisen during the course of evolution from separate polypeptides encoded by adjacent genes.
source: The close relationship of such proteins and their corresponding genes raises the possibility that dual-targeted proteins arose during the course of evolution from separate polypeptides but adjacent genes.
evidence: This is speculated based on the relationship between dual-targeted proteins and their separate homologues.

claim: The ancestral proteins may have been single, dual-targeted polypeptides that subsequently separated in some organisms.
source: Alternatively, the ancestral proteins may have been single, dual-targeted polypeptides that subsequently separated in some organisms.
evidence: This is an alternative speculation about the evolutionary origin of these proteins.
